dog.now.why: No io in the second half: devo carries the person. quindi changes nothing about word order, unlike German also. passare is the everyday 'drop by'.

dog.past.why: Two different pasts: imperfetto voleva for the intention, passato prossimo ho dovuto for what actually had to happen. Tense sits on the doors.

dog.neg.why: Non devo can also mean mustn't, so speech says non c'è bisogno di (there's no need to). That frame is impersonal, so the I disappears.

dog.q.why: No question word and no inversion: rising pitch on the second half does it. No tu either; the -i of devi already means you.

cant.now.why: No noi: possiamo carries the we. hid becomes passato prossimo hanno nascosto, the normal spoken past; perché keeps main-clause order.

cant.past.why: The hiding came first, so it moves back to trapassato avevano nascosto. Textbooks want siamo potuti (venire takes essere); abbiamo potuto is common speech.

cant.fut.why: No 'be able to' swap: the future is just an ending on potere, potremo. Domani usually opens the sentence rather than trailing after venire.

cant.although.why: still becomes lo stesso after the verb. anche se takes the plain indicative; the bookish sebbene would force the subjunctive abbiano nascosto.

like.now.why: Back to front: il caffè is the grammatical subject and a mia sorella (to my sister) is the liker. No article before a singular relative: mia sorella.

like.neg.why: le (to her) replaces a mia sorella, and non goes before the whole le piace block, never between le and piace.

like.they.why: piace stays singular because it agrees with il caffè, not the parents. Plural relatives take the article: ai miei genitori (a + i).

like.q.why: ti (to you) at the front, same order as the statement; only rising pitch makes it a question. No do-word.

go.habit.why: Plain present vanno, same order as English. a + il fuses into al, so al mercato moves as one unit. La domenica alone also means every Sunday.

go.prog.why: Subject dropped: stanno says they. stare + gerund mirrors are going, but it's optional; vanno al mercato adesso means the same.

go.past.why: andare takes essere, not avere: sono andati. The participle agrees with them, -i for a mixed or male group, andate for women only.

go.fut.why: No will word: speech keeps the present vanno and lets domani carry the future. Andranno al mercato, with tense as a suffix, is also fine.

go.neg.why: Plain present with non before it. Non stanno andando is grammatical but odd here, so non vanno covers aren't going.

live.now.why: Present plus da: literally lives in Shillong from two years. No perfect, no auxiliary; da alone says it started and is still true.

live.past.why: Finished stretch: passato prossimo ha abitato, and da turns into per. Subject dropped; ha already says he.

live.fut.why: Not a future perfect: the future sits on saranno (it will be) three years, che links, abita stays present. Avrà abitato sounds bookish.

live.q.why: Question phrase first, then plain present abiti: da quanto tempo is the question form of da due anni. No have been, no tu.

rain.now.why: No dummy it: piove is the whole first half. prendi is the tu imperative, and l'ombrello takes the, since it's the umbrella you own.

rain.fut.why: going to rain collapses into one word: the future ending -à on pioverà does the predicting. Più tardi usually comes first.

rain.neg.why: A negative tu order uses the infinitive: non prendere, not non prendi. The first half is just non before piove.

if.real.why: se + present, then future viaggeremo: the -emo ending is English will. Both noi dropped; no article on tempo.

if.unreal.why: Subjunctive avessimo after se, conditional viaggeremmo in the main clause. One extra m separates would (viaggeremmo) from will (viaggeremo).

if.past.why: Both halves are avere + participle: avessimo avuto, avremmo viaggiato. Speech often flattens it to se avevamo tempo, viaggiavamo.
